html:
SMTO-EXE-0162 — That computer is still finishing an earlier desktop step

GUID: d9868d2a-e377-590b-954c-cfa0b7c068c1
Slug: ui-busy
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: ui

What happened

  • SMTO can do only one desktop step at a time on that computer, and an earlier one hasn't finished yet. This step was not started.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait a minute, then ask SMTO in the conversation to try this step again. The Gateway accepts a new step as soon as the earlier one actually finishes, and this step never started.
  2. Make sure only one task at a time is working in apps on that computer. Two tasks controlling the same desktop would interfere, so the Gateway handles one step at a time.
  3. Look at that computer's screen for a frozen app or open dialog, and close it if that's safe. A frozen app can keep the earlier step from finishing.

What success looks like

  • SMTO starts the step and reports its result in the conversation.

If it still fails

  • If it stays busy for several minutes, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway's computer; the Gateway may need a restart. Check whether the earlier step's change happened before anything repeats it.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway's UIService input gate is still held by an earlier native call (possibly one whose caller already timed out), so the new request was refused without dispatch.

What this means

  • A native UI call still held the service's single input gate, so another request could not acquire it without overlap. Only the existing explicit UI request may observe or mutate the selected desktop. Secure values stay redacted, stale references are not retargeted, and uncertain native input is not automatically repeated.

Why this can happen

  • A native UI call still held the service's single input gate, so another request could not acquire it without overlap.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the original active call and its actual native completion; a timeout does not itself release the gate.

How to fix it

  • Wait for the earlier native call to return and release the UIService input gate, and do not send concurrent UI requests to the same Gateway. If the gate stays held, the native call is hung in the target app or OS API: inspect the Gateway log, restart the Gateway service only as a last resort, and reconcile the earlier action's effect.
  • Wait for the current native call to release its input gate. Do not submit concurrent UI mutations.

Retry and execution caution

  • Wait for the current native call to release its input gate. Do not submit concurrent UI mutations.

How to verify the fix

  • The original native call returns and releases the gate before another request is admitted.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, read secure fields, record input or bypass OS permissions.

Technical notes

  • Only the existing explicit UI request may observe or mutate the selected desktop. Secure values stay redacted, stale references are not retargeted, and uncertain native input is not automatically repeated.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
